0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 26 July 1982, after the draft finalized by the Aircraft Electrical Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council.
0.2 This standard covers the general requirements for dc motors intended for use in aircraft. 0.3 This standard shall be read in conjunction and methods of tests

with IS : 8946-1978". assistance has issued by the

0.4 In the preparation of this been derived from `BS : 2G-146 British Standards Institution.

standard, considerable DC motors for aircraft',

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This methods aircraft.
1.2 This standard specifies the general aspects of tests and performance requirements standard does not cover engine starter of design, construction, of dc motors for use in motors.

3.1.3.1 The arrangement for cooling, mounting and drive shall be as agreed upon between the manufacturer and the purchaser, but otherwise generally shall conform to IS : 8946-19787. 3.1.3.2 There shall preferably be no limitation in the performance of Such the motor in respect of the altitude in which it may be mounted. limitation, if any, shall be declared. 3.1.4 The design IS : 8946-1978T.

3.1.4.1 The design

3.1.4.2 Electrical connections - Terminals shall be provided of the connecting leads of winding and input supply terminals.

3.1.4.3 Provision shall be made in the terminal box for effecting changes in the direction of rotation in the case of reversible motor. Clear and permanent indication of correct connection in conformity with the marking practices of IS : 4728-1975* shall be given in the terminal box including marking for reversing. 3.1.4.4 Provision shall be made for internal radio interference suppression in the motor, or attachment suitable for screened cable shall be given. Any coil or winding connected in series with the armature shall preferably be disposed symmetrically in the armature circuit. 3.1.4.5 The starting system shall be simple, efficient and robust.

,6.1 Type Tests 6.1.1 Preliminary Inspection - The principal components of the motor shall be dimensionally checked against the relevant drawings ano a A check shall be made to record made of the parts liable to wear. .ensure that the brushes are bedded over the full arc for at least 80 5

IS:10237 - 1982
Any running required to condition the percent of their axial width. commutator surface shall be done prior to the commencement of the tests. Insulation resistance shall also be measured before the commencement of other tests. The weight of the motor, the distance of its centre of gravity from the mounting flange, and the polar moment of inertia of the rotor shall be determined. Checks to ensure conformity with requirements specified in IS : 8946-1978* shall be made. 6.1.2 Cold Resistance Test - The cold resistance of all the windings shall be measured at room terrperature corrected to standard temperature of 27�C ( see IS : 196-lS66t ) and checked for conformity with declared value. 6.1.3 Load Test

6.1.3.1 For a range of output torques from zero to 150 percent of' the rated torque, the current and speed shall be measured at the maximum and minimum terminal voltages specified in IS : 7854-1575$,, or as specified in the individual specification. 6.1.3.2 If the motor is reversible, these tests shall be made for both the directions of rotation. The currents and speeds shall be plotted on a torque domain and the values at rated torque thus derived for each direction of rotation shall be within * 5 percent of their respective average value. 6.1.3.3 The efficiency plotted on torque base. and output power shall be calculated and

6.1.3.4 In case the motors are supplied complete with gears, the tests laid down in 6.1.3.1 to 6.1.3.3 shall also be carried out with the gearing removed. The efficiency of the gearing at var;`cus torques shall be derived and plotted. the armature locked against rotation,. 6.1.4 Stall Test - With measurements of current and torque shall be recorded and the vaiues. range of applied voltage from zero to maximum or as plotted over high as is practicable without overheating or deterrent damage to. winding. The test shall be repeated with the armature locked in several other positions. 6.1.5 Temperature Test

6.1.5.1 For the purpose of this test, the continuous rated motors shall' be run witl-out stopping, at the rated torque and n aximum test voltage applied for a period until steady state temperature condition is reached.. Short time rated motors shall be run continuously at rated torque and

6.1.8 Insulation Resistance Test - At the conclusion of the overload tests and at the same time when the windings are hot, the insulation resistance of each of the windings shall be measured at a dc voltage of 500 V; the value obtained shall not be less than 2 megohms. 6.1.9 Altitude Test

6.1.9.1 Under conditions of air temperature, pressure, humidity and cooling applicable to its duty at the values normally prevailing at the maximum rated altitude, the motor shall function at maximum voltage and rated torque for a period of 100 h in 10 cycles of ten hours each, .each cycle being preceded by 2 h of run at sea level condition.
6.1.9.2 Intermittently rated motors shall be tested under the relevant load conditions and duty cycle specified and the temperature records during the test shall be maintained.

6.1.10 Endurance Test
6.1.10.1 Prior to the commencement of this test, the dimensions of parts liable to wear shall be measured and the ambient temperature X'o maintenance or major adjustment of any kind shall be noted. performed on the motor during this test, except that new brushes, if necessary, shall be fitted. Reversible motors shall be tested in each directicn of rotation for 50 percent of the total test period.
6.1.10.2 follows: The motor shall be subjected to test for a period as

a) Continuous duty - A total of 10 hours run followed

running period by 2 h rest.

of 1000 hours

in cycles running period

b) Motors offrequent and infrequent dub nature - A minimum period of 75 h with at least 25 one hour cooling cycles. c) Limited life - Running for 5 percent of the total specified in (a) and (b) as appropriate. running

6.1.10.3 At the conclusion of tests in 6.1.10.1 and 6.1.10.2, the insulation resistance of the motor shall be measured (when the windings are in hot condition itself ); and it shall not be less than 1 megohm. Failure to obtain this value shall be explored thoroughiy and record in detail shall be made. 6.1.10.4 The motor shall be run at no load and rated load conditions Also, the rrotor shall be examined and the current and speed recorded. for any unusual M ear and obvious visual defects of the components. 6.1.11 Acceleration Test - The motor shall function satisfactorily after being rubjccteo to acceleraticn tett as specified in the incividual cquipment specification. 6.1.12 Vibration lest - The motor shall being subjected to vibraticn test as rpeclfied specification. 8 function satisfactorily after in the indivicual equipment

6.1.13 Temperature, Pressure Test 6.1.13.1 The motor shall function satisfactorily when subjected to pressure, temperature appropriate to the classification grading declared by the manufacturer as specified in IS : 8252 ( Part II )-1980*.
6.1.13.2 During the functioning tests for the appropriate category, the motor shall be run at average speed for a few minutes to ensure that all moving parts and brushes are free. For the low temperature functioning tests, the temperature of the chamber may be lowered so that the motor is at its minimum declared ambient temperature. 6.1.13.3 Insulation resistance and after the tests in 6.1.13.2. 6.1.14 Environmental Tests and shall of the motor shall be measured before

6.2.10 Endurance Test - The test shall be carried out on representative taken from production batches, and shall be as specified samples in 6.1.10. 6.3 Number of Samples for Type Tests and Criterion for - The number of samples to be taken for type tests and Conformity during productlon tests shall be as specified by the type approving If a sample fails during any of the tests, it shall be closely authority. inspected and dismantled, and if necessary, a report on the probable cause of failure shall be made to the approving authority. With the approval of the approving authority, the test may be repeated on not more than one additional sample during type test and not more than two additional samples from each production batch, before a final decision on acceptance/rejection is taken.
